item.title: Michigan school sold for $40,000 in 2011 now asks $450,000 after one wing became 5 homes
item.description: A former school at Michigan’s K.I. Sawyer Air Force Base has undergone a striking transformation since selling for $40,000 in 2011. The 39,000-square-foot property now features five homes in one renovated wing and is listed for $450,000. Spread across 19.38 acres, the unusual property still includes classrooms, a gym, garages and spaces awaiting renovation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Lilah Mehta, the Connecticut high-school student who entered a Yale lab at 16
item.description: In a groundbreaking achievement, high school student Lilah Mehta has co-authored a significant neuroscience study, diving deep into the world of biological inquiries. Her research, which centered on ion channels potentially related to neurodegenerative diseases, led to a peer-reviewed publication. Overcoming laboratory challenges and grasping complex molecular principles, Mehta has firmly established her passion for both medicine and environmental science.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Donald Trump calls Maria Bartiromo a ‘true warrior’ after Fox News exit, says fans ‘will not be happy’
item.description: Donald Trump has praised Maria Bartiromo as a “true warrior” following her departure from Fox News Media, saying he “can’t believe” she will no longer host her shows. Trump also warned that her many fans “will not be happy.” Bartiromo’s exit comes after more than 12 years with Fox, though her lawyer disputes reports that she was fired.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Joseph Martinek bought a Texas farm in 1911; 115 years later, family protects 470 acres
item.description: Joseph Martinek purchased a Texas farm in 1911, beginning a family legacy that has lasted 115 years. In 2026, his descendants permanently protected 470 acres outside La Grange through a donated conservation easement. The property preserves farmland, wildlife habitat, open space, water resources and archaeological history while allowing the family to retain ownership and continue stewardship.

item.title: A pigeon with a ‘bleeding heart’ has returned after 20 years in Philippines, but its comeback may not be good news
item.description: In a stunning turn of events, a Mindoro bleeding-heart pigeon, a critically endangered species, has been photographed for the first time in twenty years. This sighting, occurring in the vibrant Puerto Galera rainforest on Mindoro island, confirms the species still thrives in its natural habitat. The joint efforts of indigenous patrollers and conservationists highlight the importance of protecting the fragile ecosystem that supports this rare bird.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 1989, Detroit Zoo began saving lost snails; 37 years later, 500 head 5,000 miles to Tahiti
item.description: Hundreds of tiny snails are journeying over 5,000 miles from Michigan to Tahiti. This release is part of a long-running international conservation program for endangered native snails. Invasive predators had caused severe population collapses for these unique mollusks in their native islands. The Detroit Zoo has been breeding and caring for these snails since 1989. This ongoing effort has successfully returned over 17,000 snails to their natural habitat.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Gold miners breached 14 hectares of Indonesia's orangutan refuge in three years; conservationists want government to intervene
item.description: The Jantho forest reservation in Indonesia, vital for orangutan rehabilitation, is under siege from illegal gold miners. This encroachment places the habitat of critically endangered Sumatran orangutans, rescued from illegal trade, at severe risk. Mining activities have already destroyed approximately fourteen hectares, while toxic runoff threatens the surrounding Krueng Aceh River, endangering both community health and wildlife.

item.title: California oil field faces $20 million funding gap in 25-year fight to stop development
item.description: West Coyote Hills, a 510-acre former oil field in Fullerton, California, has faced development pressure for five decades. After 25 years of efforts to preserve the land, a plan is now close to completion. California has approved a $95 million purchase of the remaining site, with $75 million already committed. Supporters are seeking the final $20 million to permanently protect the habitat as parkland and a nature preserve.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 1978, New York advocates sought affordable homes; nearly 50 years later, 145-home community is complete
item.description: After more than four decades of hurdles, a housing initiative from Long Island, initiated in 1978, has finally come to fruition with 145 affordable homes at Matinecock Court. This $98 million project overcame extensive legal and political challenges since its inception, which is linked to a pivotal Fair Housing Act case that reached the Supreme Court.

item.title: In 2002, South Australia sank ex-HMAS Hobart in under 3 minutes; 18 years later...
item.description: Having been decommissioned and sunk in 2002, the ex-HMAS Hobart has evolved into a lively underwater ecosystem. This former Australian warship is now home to more than fifty distinct fish species, while its submerged structure nurtures an array of filter-feeding organisms. Located in a safeguarded marine park sanctuary, it offers an enticing destination for divers eager to explore successful efforts in habitat rehabilitation.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Billionaire heiress Isabel Getty, great-granddaughter of J. Paul Getty, marries Faris McKinnon
item.description: Billionaire dynasty heiress Isabel Getty, great-granddaughter of oil tycoon J. Paul Getty, has married British financier Faris McKinnon in an intimate London ceremony. The couple exchanged vows at Chelsea Old Town Hall before celebrating at Harry’s Bar in Mayfair. Isabel and Faris later made a stylish exit in a vintage black Rolls-Royce, accompanied by their young son Viggo.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Australia’s endangered eastern quolls welcome new joeys; after vanishing from mainland for 60 years
item.description: Australia’s endangered eastern quolls are showing signs of recovery after conservationists successfully bred captive-raised animals in Tasmania. One released female has six joeys in her pouch, offering hope for the species’ future. Eastern quolls disappeared from mainland Australia by the 1960s, largely due to habitat loss, disease, road accidents and predation.
